beats.text: You only have room for about four close people. Watch the circles.
Researchers looked at six billion phone calls between thirty-five million people.
Who you call most forms circles. About four. Then eleven. Then thirty. Then about a hundred thirty.
Your inner circle: about four people! That's all most of us keep that close.
Losing touch with the rest isn't failing. It's a limit. That's why

sources: MacCarron, Kaski & Dunbar (2016), Calling Dunbar's numbers, Social Networks 47, 151–155 (arXiv:1604.02400) – ~6 billion calls among ~35 million people (one European country, 2007); call frequency revealed layers of about 4.1, 11.0, 29.8 and 128.9 people.
Zhou, Sornette, Hill & Dunbar (2005), Discrete hierarchical organization of social group sizes, Proc. R. Soc. B 272, 439–444 – the classic 5 / 15 / 50 / 150 layers.
